old: Its root idea is two voices calling and answering, sound set against sound.
It traces back to a Greek word built from "over against" plus "voice."
It shares its deepest roots with the word "antiphon," though they took different paths into English.
clues: This kind of song traces back to an ancient Greek term built from words meaning 'over against' and 'voice, sound.'
Less purely religious than a hymn, it is a stirring song of pride or loyalty that unites a group. It started out meaning voices answering each other across a church.
Crowds rise for the national one before a big game, and it shares its ancient source with 'antiphon,' which reached English by a different route.
